review.headline: Two Maine Coons bust themselves, and Ellis throws his whole 94-point nest.
review.summary: Blair's Maine Coon got caught in a Hawk-claim clash in round 1. Blair then won the round alone just by repeating the table's honest claims. Round 2 had no Meowfia at all. The table felt that but still had to throw, picked the one player who wouldn't name his animal, and everyone lost their cards. Round 3 dealt four cats. Both Maine Coons made failed challenges and exposed themselves. Finley then showed that Casey's 'no egg on Blair' Hawk result was impossible, and Ellis banked 94 points in one throw.

rounds.recap: Blair (Maine Coon) copied Casey's Hawk claim, and the table caught the clash at once. All three CAWs came in beat 2. Before the vote, Blair challenged by naming everyone's claimed role. Every claim was true, so Blair won alone with 18 points and nobody else scored.

Everyone was Farm. The Ugly Duckling steal (Alex took Blair's 2 cards), the Eagle report and the Hawk results all checked out. Finley never named his animal, out of fear of a Coon, so the table threw small at him. Every thrown card was lost.

Four Meowfia against two Farm. Alex's Coon challenge failed early, then Blair's failed when only Drew's Falcon guess was wrong. Blair's death proved the 'Pigeon egg in Ellis' was a lie. Finley pointed out that a real Hawk visiting a Coon must gain an egg, which broke Casey's claim. Ellis and Finley threw 21 cards to Casey and Drew's 9, and Casey was eggsecuted.

highlights.text: Blair was caught red-handed as a fake Hawk and still won alone, because the Coon challenge just read back the Farm's truthful claims.
Blair worked out that Casey was a fellow cat from the fake Hawk check, bet on it, and missed the perfect guess only on Drew.
Finley's one-line proof (a Hawk visiting a Coon must gain an egg, and Casey's nest never moved) decided the round.
Ellis threw all 12 cards at Casey and banked 94, more than everyone else combined.

confusions.what: Casey claimed that throwing at Alex 'may decide nothing' because Alex was already dead from a failed Coon bet. Ellis and Finley said it was a guaranteed win. The rules don't say whether a player who lost exclusively can be eggsecuted, or what that would mean for Farm, so nobody could settle it.

Ellis called Finley 'slow to say Pigeon'. Finley was deliberately not naming animals as an anti-Coon tactic. The rules give Farm no reason to hide roles except the Coon, and the table punished it as a cat tell.

Alex's Coon challenge assumed he was the only cat. But Drew's 'Falcon' claim reported Alex's real visit, which a House Cat could also know. Alex also bet that Casey was a Hawk while three players claimed the two Hawk cards.

Drew planned to throw one high card for the consolation and then threw all 8 cards into a vote he expected to lose. He dropped from 8 points to 1, so he seemed to underrate how expensive losing throws are.

design_notes: The Maine Coon is backwards in round 1. Once caught, it profits from the Farm's honesty, so the best Farm play wins Meowfia the round. The fix players tried (Finley hiding his animal in round 2) got an honest player eggsecuted. Consider making the challenge illegal after the day ends, or requiring it before any CAW.

No-Meowfia rounds are a pure tax. In round 2 everyone suspected there were no cats, but the minimum 1-card throw still forced a vote, and every thrown card was lost. A 'nobody' vote, or keeping cards when there are no Meowfia, would make this a real call instead of a wasted round.

Score growth makes the last round decide the game. Nests grow, so round 3 throws dwarf everything earlier: 94 points from one throw against 18 from a whole round-1 win. Consider capping banked cards or scaling earlier rounds.

Failed Coon challenges were the best engine of the game. Each reveal handed Farm hard facts: Blair's death broke the Pigeon alibi, and that broke Casey's Hawk check. But spell out what happens if a player who already lost exclusively gets the most votes.

The independent 1-in-3 roll gave 1, 0 and 4 cats across the three rounds. Two Hawks in the pool allowed triple Hawk claims, which made good cover. Also, the app prints the nest-size line twice every day.
review.title: Two Maine Coons Bust
